folds.text: **Git** keeps a history of your project. Each **commit** is a save point you can return to. It is the best undo button for anything Claude changes.
Commit before a big task. If Claude goes the wrong way, you can compare to that clean save point and go back to it. A **branch** lets you try something without touching the main copy.
Claude Code works with git in plain language. You can ask it what changed, to write a commit message, or to make a new branch. Read what it proposes before you approve.
Claude Code also keeps **checkpoints** of files it edits, and `/rewind` can restore them. They are quick session undo, not a replacement for git.
Checkpoints miss files changed only by shell commands, and changes made outside the session. Git catches those, so commit often.
